clue.text: Functions of breaks, taking pa away?

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so these letters come out of the longer word
with taking, says the named letters are removed from the word for breaks

parts.note: breaks in play or speech are pauses
the word pa is given as written

explanation.surface: A question about what interruptions are for, with father removed from the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Uses are purposes or roles, the jobs a thing performs.

clue.text: Get up with the lark

parts.note: reads as rising early, but means climbing high into the sky as a lark does when it sings

explanation.surface: Advice to rise early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up with the lark' is an idiom for waking at dawn; here it is taken literally, the lark being a bird famous for climbing steeply while singing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise high in the air, as a skylark does in its song flight.

clue.text: Weak, being one minute inside record

indicators.note: being inside means placed within, so these letters go into the record

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone feeble, having spent a minute within a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy or lacking strength, so feeble.

clue.text: Constellation seen in Arizona

explanation.surface: A star group that can be viewed from the American Southwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix is a southern constellation named after the mythical firebird, and also the state capital of Arizona.

clue.text: Lower part produces impure note

indicators.note: impure means adulterated or mixed, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A bottom section that gives a false musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: The peritoneum is the membrane lining the abdomen, a lower part of the body's trunk.

clue.text: Surprises, this season, coming out

indicators.note: coming out suggests emerging in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something unexpected appearing this season, like a debut.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze or stun, a stronger kind of surprising.

clue.text: He will petition, even when catching cold

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'He will petition, even when catching cold' (9): 'catching cold' asks for a C inside, but SUPPLIANT has no C, and no parse of 'even when' yields the answer; the clue appears to belong to a variant wording.
annotationWithheld.clue: He will petition, even when catching cold

clue.text: Lines of people waiting, we hear, for prompts

indicators.note: we hear marks that the word is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: lines of people waiting their turn are queues

explanation.surface: Asking about queues of people heard of, standing in for reminders.
explanation.definitionFit: Cues are signals telling a performer when to speak or act.

clue.text: Coward's procession has everyone up

parts.note: names a Noel Coward play that is also a parade where all the riders are up on horseback

explanation.surface: A timid person's march in which everyone stands.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was an English playwright; 'up' is horse-racing jargon for being in the saddle, so everyone is mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a procession of riders on horseback, and the title of a 1931 Coward play.

clue.text: Get rid of old car in tip

parts.note: to get rid of something is to scrap it
a heap is slang for an old run-down car

explanation.surface: Instruction to dispose of an old car at the dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip in Britain is a rubbish dump, where junk is piled.

clue.text: Silver ring in the past

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A silver ring from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, back in time.

clue.text: A third of the volume I had found worthless

indicators.note: a third of the six-letter word means its first two letters

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Finding that a third of a book's volume was of no value.
explanation.definitionFit: A void contract or ticket is null, of no value or force.

clue.text: Pulse, though almost imperceptible, felt by princess

definitions.text: though almost imperceptible, felt by princess

explanation.surface: A heartbeat so faint only royalty could feel it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition recalls the fairy tale in which a real princess feels a single tiny seed under a pile of mattresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is an edible seed of a legume, and in the fairy tale the princess was bruised by one under her bedding.

clue.text: A crop hail-damaged within a narrow field

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crop ruined by hail inside a small field.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means limited in outlook, confined to a small local sphere.

clue.text: Gluttons on watch for boar-hunter

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits atop the second

parts.note: greedy eaters are called pigs
ticker is slang for a watch

explanation.surface: Greedy eaters on guard duty for a wild-pig hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsticker hunts wild boar on horseback with a spear.

clue.text: River taking Tarka, say, over barrier to port

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: Tarka is the otter in Henry Williamson's novel Tarka the Otter
a dam is a barrier across water

explanation.surface: A river carrying a famous otter over a weir to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam in the Netherlands is one of the world's largest seaports.

clue.text: Barber's shop that overcharges?

parts.note: a hair-cutting place is a joint for clipping, and to clip is also slang for swindling customers

explanation.surface: A hairdresser who charges too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip joint is a club or bar that grossly overcharges its patrons.

clue.text: Behold love on the king's face

indicators.note: on means added after, so the king's letter follows

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning behold
love is zero in tennis, O
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A command to see love upon a monarch's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behold' wants to be the definition but supplies LO; 'face' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A face, as in a pulled expression, is a look someone gives.

clue.text: Self-vaunting exercise, for example, going on a round tour

parts.note: O is round in shape
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: A boastful jaunt, such as going on a circular tour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done to boost one's own vanity.

clue.text: Comrade may rave round making a song and dance

parts.note: a comrade is a pal

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters of rave are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend may rant about something, causing a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means a fuss or rigmarole, as does the idiom song and dance.

clue.text: Nurses a teetotaller with resolutions

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal
resolutions as conclusions are ends

explanation.surface: Nursing staff include a non-drinker with New Year resolutions.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to attend to or look after them.

clue.text: What restricts one's looking out from crow's-nest, yelling?

indicators.note: out from says the letters are taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: A lookout's view from the crow's-nest is blocked by shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'crow's-nest' and the start of 'yelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a swelling on the eyelid that can obstruct sight.

clue.text: High winds in Blackburn

explanation.surface: Gales sweeping a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackburn is a town in Lancashire; split as black + burn, black is jet and a burn is a Scottish stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast band of wind high in the atmosphere, and jet black plus burn (a brook) gives the second reading.

clue.text: Blimey! Upside down legendary flier

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise like blimey

explanation.surface: Exclaiming in surprise at a flying creature turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian tales such as Sinbad.

clue.text: Greek character wearing ring on right hand

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the ring follows the right hand

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A Greek person wearing a ring on the right hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Tart in such a house party?

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals at a party in a certain kind of house.
explanation.walkthrough: Acid house was a late-1980s dance music scene known for big warehouse parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid means sour or sharp-tasting, and acid house is a style of electronic dance music.

clue.text: New choice before important game

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: key means important

explanation.surface: A fresh selection before a vital match.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a team sport played on ice with sticks and a puck.

clue.text: City in neat stone

indicators.note: in means the city goes inside the animal

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
NY is short for New York City

explanation.surface: A city set in tidy stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy, but it is an archaic noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Dungeon guard

explanation.surface: A prison cell and its warder.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a castle's central tower, often holding a dungeon, and to keep is to protect or retain.

clue.text: Get striker out of royal house

explanation.surface: Have a player dismissed from the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the striker is the batsman facing; to york him is to bowl him with a yorker, a ball pitched at his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: York means to dismiss a batsman with a full-length ball, and the House of York was an English royal dynasty.

clue.text: Expression of male following better half

indicators.note: following means the male comes after the half
half of the six-letter word means here its last three letters

explanation.surface: A man's way of speaking after his wife has had her say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse but means half of the word 'better'.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word or phrase used to name something.

clue.text: Bed-rest day ordered for noted picnickers

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A day of bed rest prescribed for well-known outdoor diners.
explanation.walkthrough: The song The Teddy Bears' Picnic makes these toys famous for picnics.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy bears are soft toys celebrated in the song about their woodland picnic.
